content.title: About
content.content: The crab cake sandwich is a sandwich featuring a patty made from crab meat, usually served on a soft bun with lettuce, tartar sauce or mayo, and sometimes topped with avocado or tomato slices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Crab cakes are often made from a blend of crab meat, breadcrumbs, eggs, and seasonings.
The classic recipe originated in New England, USA, where crab is a regional delicacy.
The sandwich can be served hot or cold, making it a versatile snack or meal.
Mustard, lemon juice, and fresh dill are common flavor enhancers in the patty.
Crab cake sandwiches are popular at seaside restaurants and food trucks in coastal towns.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Crab meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other seafood, crab contains relatively little saturated fat.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Crab is a good source of zinc, selenium, and copper, which support immune function and metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Crab supplies vitamin B12 and B6, important for nervous system health and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Small amounts of omega‑3 in crab meat contribute to heart health.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to crab.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared crab cakes often contain added salt, so people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Crab must be fresh and stored properly to avoid salmonella or other infections.

items.title: High cholesterol in sauces
items.content: Mayonnaise‑based sauces can increase the sandwich’s cholesterol level.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The crab cake sandwich is typically cut in half and eaten by hand. It can be enhanced with fresh veggies, avocado slices, a squeeze of lemon, or a spicy sauce to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Uncooked crab cakes keep 2‑3 days refrigerated and up to 2 months frozen.

content.title: About
content.content: Crackers with cheese, reduced sodium are crunchy biscuits topped with a thin layer of melted cheese that contains less salt. They are ideal for people who watch their sodium intake but still want the taste of cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The lower sodium level is achieved through specialized processing and salt substitutes.
The cheese used is often a blend of mild and semi‑hard varieties, giving the crackers a creamy flavor.
These crackers are commonly served as a snack with soups, salads, or wine tastings.
The product is packaged in airtight bags that keep it crisp and fresh for up to 12 months.

items.title: Reduced sodium intake
items.content: Lower salt content helps maintain normal blood pressure for those monitoring sodium consumption.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cheese coating provides a modest amount of calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Cheese adds both dairy and plant‑based protein, contributing to satiety.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The dairy component may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Not suitable for individuals allergic to casein or other milk proteins.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Although salt is reduced, the cheese layer contains saturated fats; moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the crackers as a standalone snack, pair them with vegetable sticks, dips, or add them to salads for extra crunch. Their sturdy packaging makes them convenient for on‑the‑go consumption.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place, keeping the package tightly sealed. For extended storage (over 6 months), refrigeration is recommended to prevent fat oxidation.

green-beans-fresh-cooked-no-added-fat.title: Green beans, fresh, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Green beans (snap beans) are young pods of the common bean harvested before the seeds fully mature. When boiled without added fat they retain a crisp texture, a mild sweet flavor, and most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans belong to the legume family and are relatives of peas, lentils, and soy.
They contain more vitamin K than most other vegetables.
In Japan they are often served as “edamame” – lightly salted boiled pods.
Archaeological evidence shows bean cultivation dating back over 7,000 years.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: One cup of boiled green beans provides about 35 kcal, making them an excellent diet-friendly food.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and is essential for collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is crucial for DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Minerals: iron and magnesium
items.content: Iron supports oxygen transport, while magnesium contributes to muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to legumes, including green beans.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce mineral absorption; a short soak before cooking lowers its level.

items.title: Possible gas formation
items.content: Legumes can cause bloating in sensitive people; introduce them gradually into the diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boil green beans in lightly salted water for 5‑7 minutes until tender, then serve as a side dish, add to salads, soups, or stews. They can also be quickly sautéed in a dry pan without oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh pods in the refrigerator in a perforated bag for 3‑5 days. Store cooked beans in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days.

macaroni-or-pasta-salad-with-cheese.title: Macaroni or Pasta Salad with Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni or pasta salad with cheese is a cold dish where cooked pasta (or other shapes) is tossed with grated cheese, vegetables and a dressing. Common cheeses include cheddar, mozzarella or processed cheese, and dressings are often mayonnaise, sour cream or yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is popular in the United States as “pasta salad” and is a staple at picnics and barbecues.
The combination of pasta and cheese makes the salad filling enough to serve as a side or a main course.
Variations may add ham, chicken, olives, cherry tomatoes, cucumber or green onions.
Short‑shaped pasta such as shells, penne or farfalle holds the dressing better.
Cheese not only adds flavor but also provides calcium and protein.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Cheese and pasta together supply both dairy and plant protein, important for tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Hard cheeses are rich in calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Carbohydrates from pasta give a quick source of energy, useful for active individuals.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cheese and whole‑grain pasta contain B1, B2 and B12 vitamins that aid metabolism.

items.title: Probiotics (when using yogurt)
items.content: If the dressing is made with plain yogurt, it can provide beneficial bacteria for digestion.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with milk protein intolerance or lactose sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Creamy dressings and cheese make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Cheese and ready‑made dressings often contain a lot of salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial growth
items.content: If left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, the salad can develop harmful bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pasta salad chilled or slightly cool. Add fresh vegetables, herbs and a light dressing. It pairs well with grilled meat, fish, or can be enjoyed on its own as a light meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing. Discard if it develops an off smell or discoloration.

rice-brown-with-vegetables-soy-based-sau.title: Brown Rice with Vegetables and Soy Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice with vegetables and soy sauce is a ready‑to‑eat dish containing whole‑grain rice, a mix of carrots, broccoli, bell pepper and onion, tossed in a soy‑based sauce made from fermented soybeans. The meal provides complex carbohydrates, fiber, B‑vitamins and plant protein.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains the bran and germ, giving it more nutrients than white rice.
Traditional soy sauce is fermented with microbes, creating its distinctive umami flavor.
Vegetables are usually steamed, preserving most of their vitamins and minerals.
The dish is popular in vegetarian and vegan diets as a source of protein and iron.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index than white rice, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The bran in brown rice supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Plant‑based protein source
items.content: Combined rice and soy sauce provide a complete set of essential amino acids.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Contains magnesium, phosphorus and iron, supporting muscle function and blood health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Helps control blood glucose levels, beneficial for people with pre‑diabetes.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Soy sauce can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce often contains a lot of salt; those with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Brown rice contains phytic acid, which may reduce mineral absorption if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The dish is ready to eat after reheating. Serve it as a standalone meal, add to salads, use in wraps, or pair with tofu or fish as a side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days or freeze portions for longer storage.

content.title: About
content.content: Taquito are small crunchy rolls made from a corn or wheat tortilla, filled with tender chicken fillet, spices and sometimes vegetables. The product is popular in Mexican cuisine as a quick snack or appetizer.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Taquito are often served with salsa, guacamole or sour cream.
Traditionally the rolls are made from corn tortillas, but some regions use a wheat base.
The chicken filling is usually marinated in chili, paprika and lime spices.
In the United States Taquito are frequently sold frozen, ready for microwave or oven heating.
The name “taquito” comes from the Spanish word meaning “little taco”.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken meat is a good source of high‑quality protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other snacks, chicken Taquito contain less saturated fat, especially when prepared without excess oil.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken provides vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: The product supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bones.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Chicken meat is considered easy to digest, making Taquito a suitable snack for children and older adults.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to poultry, experiencing skin reactions or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made Taquito often contain added salt and sauces, increasing sodium levels.

items.title: Trans fats in coating
items.content: Industrial breadings may contain trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Risk of food poisoning
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking of chicken can lead to bacterial growth such as salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Taquito can be heated in the oven, microwave or skillet until golden and crisp. Serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream or fresh lime. They are convenient to eat by hand as a snack or added to a salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen Taquito in the freezer at –18 °C. After thawing, cook immediately. Cooked rolls can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days.
